A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learning the Minimum Action Distance by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison and matching of relocated content.

before.justification: v3 reports original distance-learning experiments, ablations, maze visualizations, and downstream planning success rates in Section 7 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, architecture and loss ablations, and teleport-environment results.

M1.justification: MadDist, TDMadDist, the simple quasimetric, and the target-network update retain their procedures. Renaming L_o to L_tau, clarifying successor notation, and explaining already-supported quasimetrics do not establish algorithm changes; numerical hyperparameter revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: v4 adds an AntMaze teleport evaluation with deterministic, directed teleport transitions, documented in Appendix H and plotted in Figure 16. The earlier grid worlds, maze environments, and Navigate, Stitch, and Explore coverage remain.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates QRL and Hilbert as baselines. v4 adds PlanDist and PlanDist-Simple to both distance-learning comparisons and all seven planning comparisons in Table 1. These introduce the closely related predecessor and a control using the proposed quasimetric with the predecessor's objective.

E3.justification: Tables 2–3 change the reported constraint weight from 0.1 to 0.01; MadDist's listed contrastive weight and maximum distance become 10 and 500. MediumMaze curves extend from 50,000 to 100,000 steps, while teleport experiments use 200,000. New architecture controls and evaluations across ground-truth-distance cutoffs also expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.4 tests three QRL architectures and two Hilbert architectures on CliffWalking. New Appendix F tests contrastive weight on AntMaze Navigate and Explore, and constraint horizon on Explore. These investigate capacity confounds and objective components beyond the retained latent-size, quasimetric-choice, and dataset-size ablations.

E5.justification: Section 7, Figure 3, and the planning protocol change their stated seed count from three to five. v3's appendix plots already specified five seeds, so the PDFs establish revised reporting without resolving exactly which experiments received additional runs. Existing min–max shading and Table 1 standard-deviation reporting remain.

E6.justification: v4 adds baseline, teleport, architecture, and loss-ablation results and revises distance-learning curves. Table 1 adds 14 entries, including PlanDist's 0.19±0.22 and PlanDist-Simple's 0.05±0.12 on AntMaze Medium Explore; all 28 existing mean/standard-deviation entries remain identical. Revised settings prevent interpreting curve changes as straightforward same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the assertion that every reachable one-step pair has distance one by excluding identical states. The pointwise-maximality statement and embedding reduction largely restate mathematics already present in v3 Appendices A and C, whose proofs remain. Section 5 additionally supplies explicit Wide Norm and IQE constructions.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly claims greater learning efficiency than existing methods and improved downstream goal-reaching, whereas v3 emphasized representation accuracy. The same two algorithms, simple quasimetric, and controlled benchmark suite remain the central contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations attributing gains beyond asymmetry to the revised objective, explaining contrastive supervision under weak trajectories and longer constraints through local geometric consistency. It clarifies discrete decision steps versus physical time and sharpens the existing planning-diagnostic framing. However, Section 4 removes v3's explicit rare-transition caveat and detailed comparison with stochastic shortest paths.

D1.justification: Appendix D.6 and Table 6 document PlanDist architectures, distances, optimization, and hyperparameters. Appendix H specifies teleport mappings, episode filtering, and BFS ground-truth construction. v4 also identifies a repository for a future code release, replacing v3's unspecified release-upon-acceptance promise; actual availability is not established.

R1.justification: v4 adds Sutton, Precup, and Singh (1999) for the semi-Markov discussion and sharpens its relationship to the already-cited Steccanella and Jonsson (2022) through PlanDist comparisons. Most related-work discussion and cited works remain; extensive bibliographic capitalization and formatting edits do not change positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and Sections 3–5 receive substantial rewriting and expanded explanations, including bringing existing appendix mathematics into the main narrative. Loss terminology changes, the experimental discussion expands, and new appendix sections reorganize the later material. These changes substantially revise the exposition despite stable proposed algorithms.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 8–12 and Table 6, expands Table 1 with two columns, and revises comparison-plot legends and panels. Figure 3 changes from three rows to two and replaces Giant Navigate with Giant Stitch. Original ablation graphics and maze visualizations are retained and relocated, while the AntMaze results gain a teleport row.

improvement.justification: v3 lacked direct evaluation against its closest trajectory-loss predecessor and tests isolating important objective components. v4 addresses these central validation gaps through PlanDist/PlanDist-Simple comparisons and the architecture, contrastive-weight, and constraint-horizon studies in Appendices E.4 and F. This substantially strengthens the evidence explaining the method's advantages. The loss of the useful rare-transition/SSP qualification is a drawback, but does not outweigh these gains.
